questions.question: What property must a material have to allow particles of a liquid to move through it by diffusion?
options: It must be permeable.
It must be magnetic.
It must be opaque.
It must be highly reflective.

questions.question: When conducting an experiment with a jelly cube placed in a coloured liquid, what process is observed as the liquid spreads into the jelly?
options: Evaporation
Diffusion
Filtration
Condensation

questions.question: If you increase the temperature of the liquid surrounding a jelly cube, what is the expected effect on the rate of diffusion into the cube?
options: Diffusion will stop completely.
Diffusion will speed up.
Diffusion will slow down.
Diffusion rate will remain exactly the same.

questions.question: If you compare diffusion into a small jelly cube versus a large jelly cube, which cube will have its centre reached by the diffusing liquid first?
options: The small cube, because the distance to the centre is shorter.
The large cube, because it has a larger surface area to attract the liquid.
Both cubes at exactly the same time.
Neither cube, as liquid cannot reach the centre of a jelly cube.

questions.question: Using particle theory, why does a higher temperature increase the rate of diffusion into a jelly cube?
options: Particles have more kinetic energy and move faster.
Particles become larger and take up more space.
Particles lose all their energy and settle down.
Particles break apart into smaller atoms.

questions.question: Why can only some substances diffuse through a selectively-permeable membrane?
options: Only some particles are small enough to pass through the tiny holes in the membrane.
Only magnetic particles can pass through the membrane.
Only particles with a positive electrical charge can pass.
Only liquid particles can pass, while all gas particles are blocked.

questions.question: When particles diffuse through a selectively-permeable membrane, in which direction do they move?
options: Only out of the membrane, never into it.
Only into the membrane, never out of it.
In both directions across the membrane.
They do not move through the membrane at all.

questions.question: If there is a higher concentration of a substance outside a selectively-permeable membrane than inside, what is the predicted direction of net movement of the particles?
options: Net movement will be into the membrane.
Net movement will be out of the membrane.
There will be no movement of particles at all.
Particles will only move along the outer surface without entering.

questions.question: In an experiment using Visking tubing to represent a cell, what indicates the net movement of water into the tubing?
options: The volume or mass of the liquid inside the tubing increases.
The Visking tubing dissolves completely.
The liquid inside the tubing changes colour to bright blue.
The tubing shrinks to half its original length.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about the cytoplasm inside a cell?
options: It is a continuous solid block that contains no individual particles.
It is made up of particles, just like all other substances.
It is made of empty space with no matter in it.
It is the only substance in a cell that is not made of particles.

questions.question: How do necessary substances like oxygen diffuse into a cell?
options: By passing through small holes in the cell membrane.
By melting the cell wall.
By being actively pushed by microscopic cellular pumps.
By converting into energy before entering.

questions.question: Why are some substances unable to diffuse into a cell through the cell membrane?
options: Their particles are too large to pass through the holes in the membrane.
Their particles are moving too quickly.
They do not have any chemical energy.
They are completely repelled by the cell's magnetic field.

questions.question: What does it mean when we say a cell membrane is 'selectively-permeable'?
options: It allows all substances to pass through freely.
It allows only some substances to diffuse through it.
It prevents any substances from entering or leaving.
It is made entirely of water.

questions.question: How do particles move during the process of diffusion?
options: In straight, organized lines without colliding.
In random directions, colliding with each other constantly.
They only move in a clockwise circular path.
They remain completely stationary.

questions.question: What is meant by the term 'concentration' in science?
options: The total mass of a single particle.
The number of particles in a given volume of liquid or gas.
The speed at which particles vibrate.
The temperature of a gas.

questions.question: What does it mean for particles to move 'down a concentration gradient'?
options: Moving from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration.
Moving from an area of lower concentration to an area of higher concentration.
Moving upwards against gravity.
Moving only in a liquid state, never in a gas.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct definition of diffusion?
options: The active transport of particles requiring energy.
The passive movement of particles from an area of higher to lower concentration.
The chemical reaction between two different liquids.
The freezing of a liquid into a solid.

questions.question: If starch solution is inside a Visking tubing bag and iodine is outside, iodine particles diffuse in and turn the starch blue-black, but starch does not diffuse out. How is this explained?
options: Iodine particles are small enough to pass through the membrane, but starch particles are too large.
Starch is attracted to the inside of the bag by gravity.
Iodine particles are actively pumped by the Visking tubing.
The Visking tubing has no holes at all.
